hypothesis: New mapped strands are enriched in the damage zone of mapped faults, with cross-strike offset, along-strike position, orientation and host-system scale carrying information beyond distance alone. This is a testable spatial association, not proof of a tectonic mechanism.
mechanism: H57 uses a gradient-boosted model over catalogue-derived distance, cross-strike and along-strike geometry, orientation, component scale, coherence and local density. Features are rebuilt from the visible catalogue for each holdout fold; visible catalogue pixels are masked exactly. The final model then allocates binary dots with the alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, 300 m triangular-kernel DTI marginal rule. Recorded slip-sense is available in the local INGENIOUS vector data but was not encoded in this candidate.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Incomplete mapping or mapper stopping mid-system can make withheld catalogue pixels appear near visible traces without representing undiscovered structure. Linear dry washes/alluvial channels, roads and ridge crests can also align with regional structural trends and mimic mapped lineaments.
